newsitem.title: USA: Ronald Reagan's brother dies of heart failure.
newsitem.headline: Ronald Reagan's brother dies of heart failure.

text.p: Neil Reagan, the older brother of former President Ronald Reagan, has died of heart failure. He was 88 years old.
Reagan, a former radio broadcaster and advertising executive, died Wednesday at Scripps Memorial Hospital in San Diego, according to a statement issued Thursday by the ex-president's office.

Known to friends and family by the nickname "Moon," he was said to have been close to his younger brother and served as a delegate to the 1980 Republican national convention that propelled Reagan to the presidency.
But Neil Reagan, the ex-president's only sibling, kept a low profile during his brother's two terms in office.

"We will miss him terribly," Reagan and his wife Nancy said. "We have been in constant contact with his wife, Bess, in the last few days and have expressed our sympathy and love. We hope all Americans will join us in our prayers for Moon and Bess."
The 85-year-old ex-president has rarely appeared in public since announcing in November 1994 he was suffering from Alzheimer's disease, an incurable and progressive brain disorder.
Like his famous brother, Neil Reagan was born in Tampico, Ill.
When Ronald Reagan enrolled at Eureka College in Eureka, Ill., he encouraged his brother to join him.
Neil Reagan graduated with a degree in economics in 1933 and married Bess Hoffman in 1935. They have no children.
When Ronald Reagan became an announcer at WHO Radio in Des Moines, Iowa, his brother followed him, becoming programme director at a sister station in Davenport.
After Ronald Reagan moved to Hollywood to pursue an acting career, his brother followed and won his first California job as a radio announcer for Los Angeles station KFWB.
He later worked for CBS and then joined the McCann-Erickson Advertising Agency, where he became senior vice president and head of the Los Angeles office until his retirement in 1973.

While with McCann-Erickson, Reagan directed actor Jean Hersholt in his famed radio role as the kindly Dr. Paul Christian and later directed his brother in the Western TV series "Death Valley Days," according to his official biography.
At the time of his death, he was living in the Rancho Santa Fe area near San Diego.
"In accordance with Neil's express wishes, he received the last rites before his death and requested that there be no public services," according to the statement from Reagan's office.
